reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
Wednesday in October. Nothing particularly happening. The leaves are doing their thing, the mornings have teeth now, and the week isn't close enough to the weekend to feel like anything. This is the day that used to grind me down the most when I was drinking — the sheer unremarkableness of it. If nothing was happening, I had to make something happen. Usually at a bar. Usually ending badly.

What I didn't understand at 22 is that most of a life is Wednesdays. Most of a career, most of a marriage, most of a friendship, most of being someone's kid or parent or neighbor — it all happens on days like this one. If you can't show up for the ordinary Wednesday, you can't actually show up for your life. You just show up for the highlights, and the highlights get thinner and thinner until there's nothing between them but static.

Sobriety taught me that the Wednesday is the whole thing. The coffee that actually tastes like coffee. The walk to the car in cold air. The call to a friend you've been meaning to call. The workout you don't feel like doing. None of it looks like much from the outside. From the inside, it's the quiet accumulation of a life you don't have to escape from.
reflection.meditation: What ordinary moment today can I actually be present for, instead of waiting through?

affirmations: I am building a life out of ordinary days, not escaping from them.
Today I can respond instead of react.
I am becoming someone I don't need a break from.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful for a Wednesday I get to be awake for. Grateful for the small stuff — the coffee, the clear head, the fact that I remember yesterday and get to show up for today. There were years I would have traded all of this for one more drink. I'm glad I don't have to anymore.
gratitude.closing: One ordinary day at a time.
